# Fraud model — evaluation report

A **trained ML fraud-scoring model evaluated on synthetic UPI-shaped data with
an external PaySim benchmark.**

That phrasing is exact and deliberate. This model is **not** production-proven,
**not** real-world validated, and **not** validated by any regulator. See
§13 before quoting any number here.

Replaces `aasthichain-rules-v1`, a hand-tuned weighted sum of eight thresholds.
No LLM is involved in any decision or any explanation.

---

## 1. Dataset provenance

**Training / evaluation data — synthetic, generated by this repository.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Generator | `ml/generate_dataset.py` |
| Seed | `20260930` (fixed, committed) |
| Rows | 139,788 payments from 40,000 payers |
| Fraud rate | 4.66% (6,519 positive) |
| Committed? | No — regenerates deterministically from the seed |

**External benchmark — PaySim.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | `https://huggingface.co/datasets/LordNR/AMLGraphX-Paysim` |
| Revision | `9dc258656e186b03c4fad26ecb02c3ca9d19c337` |
| File | `paysim.zip` → `paysim.csv` |
| Licence | CC BY-SA 4.0 — the HF repo is a redistribution, not the origin |
| Origin | *PaySim: A financial mobile money simulator for fraud detection* |
| Size | 6,362,620 rows · 8,213 frauds · 0.129% · 743 hourly steps (~31 days) |
| Schema | `step, type, amount, nameOrig, oldbalanceOrg, newbalanceOrig, nameDest, oldbalanceDest, newbalanceDest, isFraud, isFlaggedFraud` |

Schema inspected before use, not assumed. Fraud occurs **only** in `TRANSFER`
(0.769%) and `CASH_OUT` (0.184%); `PAYMENT`, `CASH_IN` and `DEBIT` are 0.000%.

---

## 2. Synthetic-data generation methodology

Labels come from the **generative process**, never from the existing rule
thresholds. Each payer is assigned a behaviour class, and the label is "was
this payer acting fraudulently in this episode". Deriving labels from the rules
would make the model relearn the rules and every comparison circular.

**Typologies injected** (all documented, all seeded):

| Typology | Shape |
|---|---|
| `structuring` | 3–8 payments of ₹45,500–49,900, just under the reporting line |
| `velocity_burst` | 7–15 payments seconds to minutes apart |
| `account_takeover` | Established account, 6–14 escalating payments draining a fixed balance |
| `mule_fan_in` | Fresh unverified beneficiary receiving from 8–30 distinct payers |
| `mule_fan_out` | One account spraying to 10–40 brand-new beneficiaries |
| `beneficiary_anomaly` | Dormant ordinary account, then one large payment to a new payee |
| `handle_mimic` | Payee handle copies the payer's local part on a different bank (impersonation) |

**Deliberate class overlap.** Honest payers who burst (`retail_busy`), honest
whales (`retail_highvalue`) and honest payments to brand-new counterparties
(`retail_new_beneficiary`) are injected on purpose. Without them the generator
yields AUC ≈ 1.0, which proves only that the generator is easy, and the model
would treat beneficiary novelty as near-proof of fraud.

**Asymmetric label noise.** 5% of fraud is relabelled legitimate (never
reported); 0.1% of legitimate is relabelled fraud (mistaken dispute). Symmetric
noise at a 4% base rate would swamp the positive class with mislabelled
negatives.

## 3. Feature list (23)

Every feature is computable from what the API holds when a collect request
arrives. A feature that cannot be computed in the request path is useless, so
none are included.

| # | Feature | Family |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `log_amount` | amount |
| 2 | `amount_in_structuring_band` | amount |
| 3 | `balance_ratio` | balance |
| 4 | `recent_in_structuring_band` | structuring |
| 5 | `recent_amount_cv` | structuring |
| 6 | `structuring_x_tightness` | structuring |
| 7 | `txn_count_10m` | velocity / rolling window |
| 8 | `txn_count_24h` | velocity / rolling window |
| 9 | `log_total_24h` | amount over rolling window |
| 10 | `amount_vs_recent_mean` | escalation |
| 11 | `burstiness` | velocity |
| 12 | `velocity_x_escalation` | account-takeover indicator |
| 13 | `beneficiary_is_new` | beneficiary novelty |
| 14 | `distinct_payees_24h` | fan-out |
| 15 | `payee_fan_in_24h` | fan-in |
| 16 | `log_account_age_min` | account standing |
| 17 | `kyc_unverified` | account standing |
| 18 | `new_account_x_amount` | account standing |
| 19 | `is_night` | time-of-day |
| 20 | `is_weekend` | day-of-week |
| 21 | `is_transfer_type` | transaction type |
| 22 | `risky_vpa_fragment` | counterparty identifier |
| 23 | `handle_mimic` | counterparty identifier / impersonation |

**Device / IP features are deliberately absent.** The brief lists them "if
available in our existing schema". They are not: no payment record carries a
device id, IP or user-agent. Synthesising them would train the model on a
signal the server can never supply.

Sender and receiver identifiers are used to *derive* features 13–15; the raw
ids are never fed to the model, as that would invite memorisation.

## 4. Training configuration

| | |
|---|---|
| Library | scikit-learn (`LogisticRegression`, lbfgs) |
| Shipped model | `aasthichain-fraud-lr-v3`, schema v3 (23 coefficients) |
| Regularisation | L2, `C=1.0` |
| Class imbalance | `class_weight="balanced"` |
| Max iterations | 5000 |
| Seed | `20260930` |
| Network calls | none |
| Inference | dot product over 22 coefficients — microseconds |
| Comparison model | `GradientBoostingClassifier`, 200 trees, depth 3 |

The scaler is folded into the exported coefficients, so serving needs no
scaler and the contribution identity holds on **raw** feature values:

```
z = Σ coefficient_i · x_i + intercept
```

The export is rejected unless it reproduces sklearn's `decision_function` over
every test row. Current deviation: **1.42e-14**.

---

## 5. Class distribution

| Split | Rows | Fraud | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Train | 84,027 | 3,811 | 4.54% |
| Validation | 27,816 | 1,402 | 5.04% |
| Test | 27,945 | 1,306 | 4.67% |

**Split is by `payer_id`, 60/20/20.** Rows within one payer's episode are
strongly correlated. A random row split puts a payer's early payments in train
and their later ones in test, leaking behaviour across the boundary and
inflating every metric. No payer appears in two splits — asserted in code.

---

## 6. Validation metrics

Threshold chosen here, on validation.

| Model | Precision | Recall | F1 | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rules-v1` (replaced) | 0.9209 | 0.2739 | 0.4222 | 0.8554 | 0.5363 |
| **Logistic regression (shipped)** | **0.9005** | **0.8452** | **0.8720** | **0.9670** | **0.8828** |
| Gradient boosting (comparison) | 0.9124 | 0.9508 | 0.9312 | 0.9838 | 0.9285 |

## 7. Held-out test metrics

Threshold carried over from validation, never re-tuned here.

| Model | Precision | Recall | F1 | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rules-v1` (replaced) | 0.9371 | 0.2282 | 0.3670 | 0.8438 | 0.4814 |
| **Logistic regression (shipped)** | **0.8888** | **0.8629** | **0.8757** | **0.9656** | **0.8842** |
| Gradient boosting (comparison) | 0.9131 | 0.9571 | 0.9346 | 0.9839 | 0.9293 |

The rules caught **23%** of fraud. The shipped model catches **86%**, and
PR-AUC — the metric that matters on imbalanced data — goes from 0.481 to 0.884.

**Accuracy is not reported anywhere.** At a 4.7% base rate, approving
everything scores 95.3%.

---

## 8. Threshold selection

| | |
|---|---|
| Policy | highest recall subject to **precision ≥ 0.90** |
| Chosen on | **validation split** |
| Block threshold | `0.848545` |
| Review threshold | `0.339418` (0.4 × block) |
| Precision floor met | yes |

A shield that blocks genuine payments destroys more value than it saves, so the
operating point is fixed by a precision floor rather than by maximising
accuracy or F1.

If the floor is unreachable, the selector falls back to the best-F1 point **and
records `precision_floor_met: false`**. An earlier version silently returned
0.5 on failure, which on PaySim's 0.3% base rate produced a 7% precision
operating point that looked like a model failure when it was a
threshold-selection failure.

## 9. Confusion matrix (test, shipped model)

|  | Predicted legit | Predicted fraud |
|---|---|---|
| **Actually legit** | 26,498 | 141 |
| **Actually fraud** | 179 | 1,127 |

141 false positives out of 26,639 legitimate payments — a 0.53% false-positive
rate. 179 frauds missed out of 1,306.

| | Validation | Test |
|---|---|---|
| ROC-AUC | 0.9670 | 0.9656 |
| PR-AUC | 0.8828 | 0.8842 |
| Brier | see `model/metrics.json` | |

PR-AUC is the headline. ROC-AUC is optimistic on imbalanced data because the
true-negative pool is enormous.

## 11. Feature coefficients

Intercept: **−7.5253**. Positive drives the score toward fraud.

| Feature | Coefficient |
|---|---|
| `handle_mimic` | +7.7590 |
| `is_transfer_type` | +5.7387 |
| `amount_in_structuring_band` | +5.0170 |
| `risky_vpa_fragment` | +3.2059 |
| `burstiness` | +2.3647 |
| `kyc_unverified` | +2.3494 |
| `structuring_x_tightness` | +1.3148 |
| `beneficiary_is_new` | +0.9615 |
| `distinct_payees_24h` | +0.7950 |
| `is_night` | +0.7491 |
| `log_account_age_min` | +0.4026 |
| `is_weekend` | +0.3007 |
| `txn_count_10m` | +0.2019 |
| `balance_ratio` | +0.1457 |
| `new_account_x_amount` | +0.1224 |
| `recent_in_structuring_band` | +0.0414 |
| `log_total_24h` | +0.0221 |
| `amount_vs_recent_mean` | +0.0043 |
| `velocity_x_escalation` | -0.0002 |
| `payee_fan_in_24h` | -0.0304 |
| `log_amount` | -0.1831 |
| `txn_count_24h` | -0.3937 |
| `recent_amount_cv` | -0.5768 |

Two coefficients are worth reading carefully rather than at face value.
`log_amount` is **negative** because amount is already carried by
`amount_in_structuring_band` and `balance_ratio`; conditional on those, a large
amount is mildly reassuring in this dataset. `payee_fan_in_24h` and
`velocity_x_escalation` are near zero because their signal is already absorbed
by `distinct_payees_24h` and `burstiness` respectively. Neither is a
claim about real fraud — they are properties of this synthetic distribution.

### Explainability

Every prediction returns:

```json
{
  "probability": 0.683, "score": 68, "decision": "REVIEW",
  "threshold": 0.847605, "baseline": -6.8059,
  "modelVersion": "aasthichain-fraud-lr-v3 (schema v3)",
  "topPositive": [
    {"code":"AMOUNT_IN_STRUCTURING_BAND","note":"amount sits just under the ₹50,000 reporting line","weight":431},
    {"code":"BENEFICIARY_IS_NEW","note":"first ever payment to this beneficiary","weight":140}
  ],
  "topNegative": [
    {"code":"LOG_AMOUNT","note":"payment size ₹47000","weight":-196}
  ]
}
```

`weight` is `feature_value × coefficient × 100`. The contributions plus the
intercept equal the logit **exactly** — asserted in Go
(`TestContributionsReconcile`), JS and Python. An explanation that does not
reconcile with the score that was acted on is decoration, so it is tested, not
assumed. No LLM is used to produce any of this text.

**Policy overrides.** Unverified KYC and phishing-style VPAs are never
auto-approved regardless of score. They appear as `POLICY_*` with weight `0`, so
an analyst can always see which part of a decision was *learned* and which was
*mandated*.

## 12. PaySim external benchmark

Same model classes, same precision-floor protocol, **chronological** split by
`step` (60/20/20), threshold chosen on validation. Restricted to `TRANSFER` and
`CASH_OUT`: 2,770,409 rows, 8,213 frauds (0.296%).

| Model | Precision | Recall | F1 | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Threshold rules | 0.4004 | 0.1430 | 0.2108 | 0.7850 | 0.0741 |
| Logistic regression | 0.5857 | 0.6498 | 0.6161 | 0.9872 | 0.5622 |
| Gradient boosting | 0.9836 | 0.7588 | 0.8567 | 0.7590 | 0.7601 |

Both models beat the rules baseline by a wide margin on PR-AUC (0.56 / 0.76 vs
0.074). **LR could not reach the 90% precision floor on PaySim** — recorded as
`precision_floor_met: false`, with the best-F1 point used instead.

### Measured domain mismatch

PaySim senders are effectively unique: in a 1.5M-row sample, **99.96% of
`nameOrig` values appear exactly once**, maximum 3. There is therefore **no
per-sender history in PaySim**, so the entire velocity / rolling-window half of
the feature family cannot be evaluated there. Destinations do repeat (17%
appear more than once, max 98), so fan-in and novelty are computable.

Transferable (10): amount, balance ratio, balance-emptied, origin balance,
destination balance, fan-in, beneficiary novelty, type, night, weekend.

Not transferable (15): all velocity and rolling-window features, all
structuring features (no ₹ reporting line), KYC, VPA, account age.

So PaySim benchmarks **the approach on a subset of the feature family**, not the
shipped model. Its weights are discarded.

---

## 13. Limitations and domain mismatch

Read this before quoting any number above.

- **Our UPI training data is synthetic.** It was generated by this repository
  from assumptions about what fraud looks like.
- **PaySim is also synthetic.** It is a simulator, not production banking data.
- **PaySim is not UPI.** It is mobile money, with a different schema, different
  typologies and no per-sender history.
- **Real production performance requires appropriately labelled real
  UPI/payment data.** None exists in this project. Until it does, every metric
  here describes synthetic behaviour.

Further limitations:

- **The generator encodes assumptions.** A typology it does not contain is a
  typology the model has not learned.
- **No graph features.** Mule networks are a structure across accounts;
  `payee_fan_in_24h` is a crude one-hop proxy. This is the largest gap.
- **No feedback loop.** The model does not learn from analyst decisions; doing
  that needs outcome labels this system does not collect.
- **No device or IP signals**, because the schema has none.
- **Drift is unmonitored.** There is no PSI/population-stability check.
- **Known train/serve skew, found and fixed.** `balance_ratio` divided by
  `(balance + 1)`, so a *missing* balance produced the amount itself (a ratio of
  47,000 for a ₹47,000 payment) and dominated every explanation. Unknown
  balances now contribute 0 and the ratio is capped at 20. Caught by inspecting
  a live response, not by a test — which is itself a finding about test
  coverage.

### Why logistic regression ships

The gradient-boosted tree scores better on held-out synthetic data: test PR-AUC
0.929 vs 0.884, recall 0.957 vs 0.863. The linear model ships anyway because it
buys two things that outweigh ~9 points of recall for a regulated payments
decision:

- **An exact additive explanation.** `contribution = value × coefficient`, and
  those contributions plus the intercept equal the logit exactly. "Why was this
  blocked" has an arithmetic answer that reconciles, not a post-hoc
  approximation.
- **A trivially portable artifact.** 22 coefficients, no numerical subtleties.
  The tree export needs float32 narrowing to match sklearn; a dot product does
  not.

This is a documented trade-off, not an accident. The tree is exported to
`model/gbt_comparison.json` and both Go and JS can load and score it — point
`FRAUD_MODEL_PATH` at that file to serve it — so the trade-off stays
measurable rather than asserted.

---

## Serving and parity

Trained in Python, served in Go (`drunix-gateway/model.go`) and JavaScript
(`lib/fraud-model.js`). Three implementations of the same arithmetic drift
unless something forces them not to.

**200 golden vectors** carrying sklearn's logit, probability and every
per-feature contribution are committed, and both ports must match to `1e-9`:

| Implementation | Worst logit | Worst probability | Worst contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Go | 4.00e-15 | 6.11e-16 | 0 |
| JavaScript | 4.00e-15 | 6.11e-16 | 0 |

Tolerance `1e-9`; observed deviation is ~1e-15, i.e. double-precision rounding.

**Fallback.** If the artifact is missing or corrupt, Go's `ScorePaymentAuto`
falls back to the original rules engine and marks the result; the JS path
returns `engine: "rules-fallback"` with the reason. A fraud engine that
silently becomes a no-op is worse than one that is loudly degraded.

**API compatibility.** `RiskResult` keeps its original five fields
(`score`, `band`, `decision`, `factors`, `model`), so existing callers and
stored records are unaffected. Everything new is additive and `omitempty`.
`HistorySummary` gained five optional fields; a caller that does not populate
them gets zero values, which the extractor treats as "unknown".

---

## Reproducing

```bash
cd ml
python3 generate_dataset.py      # 139,788 payments, seed 20260930
python3 train.py                 # trains, verifies the export, writes artifacts
python3 test_pipeline.py         # determinism + artifact + explanation tests
python3 paysim_benchmark.py      # external benchmark (~185 MB download, not committed)
```

`train.py` refuses to export unless the folded coefficients reproduce sklearn
exactly. Both are assertions, not warnings.
